0|4594bf159f1962cec3b727954b7c598b07e2e737|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"[PATCH] WorkStruct: Use direct assignment rather than cmpxchg()
Use direct assignment rather than cmpxchg() as the latter is unavailable
and unimplementable on some platforms and is actually unnecessary.
The use of cmpxchg() was to guard against two possibilities
which can actually occur:
(1) The pending flag may have been unset or may be cleared.  However
where it's called
column2: the pending flag is _always_ set.  I don't think it

column1: can be unset whilst we're in set_wq_data().
Once the work is enqueued to be actually run
column2: the only way off the queue

column1: is for it to be actually run.
If it's a delayed work item
column2: then the bit can't be cleared by the timer

column1: because we haven't started the timer yet.  Also
cleared by cancelling the delayed work _until_ the work item has had its
timer started.
(2) The workqueue pointer might change.  This can only happen in two cases:
(a) The work item has just been queued to actually run
protected by the appropriate workqueue spinlock.
(b) A delayed work item is being queued
column2: and so the timer hasn't been

column1: started yet
column2: and so no one else knows about the work item or can

column1: access it (the pending bit protects us).
Besides
it can be assigned instead.
So
column2: replacing the set_wq_data() with a straight assignment would be okay

column1: in most cases.
The problem is where we end up tangling with test_and_set_bit() emulated
using spinlocks
column2: and even then it's not a problem _provided_

column1: test_and_set_bit() doesn't attempt to modify the word if the bit was
set.
If that's a problem
column2: then a bitops-proofed assignment will be required -

column1: equivalent to atomic_set() vs other atomic_xxx() ops.
